h3. *Feature Overview (aka. Goal Summary)*

This feature aims to ensure that once all Platform Agnostic and Rolling Streams operator teams have completed their TLS consistency/ML-KEM development and per-component testing, the resulting cluster (sum of all parts) does indeed behave as intended: TLS 1.3 with hybrid ML-KEM being the default offered key encapsulation protocol. This applies to all TLS servers of all operators *and all operands* — it is not sufficient to validate operator endpoints alone.

h3. *Goals (aka. expected user outcomes)*

A newly deployed OCP 5.0 cluster should use quantum-safe key encapsulation by default for all TLS connections served by Platform Agnostic and Rolling Streams operators *and their operands*.

h3. *Requirements (aka. Acceptance Criteria):*

Once an OCP 5.0 cluster is up and running, a CI job can scan all discoverable service endpoints exposed by Platform Agnostic and Rolling Streams operators *and their operands* to ensure they're using TLS 1.3 (required for PQC support), and then run a series of smoke tests to validate basic functionality while in PQC-mode.

h3. *Testing Approaches*

Teams should validate ML-KEM support using one or more of these approaches:

* *Cluster-wide scan* - tls-scanner periodic CI covers basic cluster installation
* *Namespace-specific scan* - Layered products should point tls-scanner at their namespace during integration testing
* *Dedicated functional tests* - Required for short-lived/transient TLS endpoints that the scanner cannot reliably catch

⚠️ The tls-scanner cannot guarantee it will find transient endpoints. Teams must add dedicated testing for any TLS servers that spin up/down during normal operations. ⚠️

ℹ️Teams must validate ML-KEM support for all TLS servers exposed by both their operator and any operands it manages. Operator-only validation is insufficient.ℹ️


*Deployment considerations:*

| *Deployment considerations* | *List applicable specific needs (N/A = not applicable)* |
| --- | --- |
| Self-managed, managed, or both | X |
| Classic (standalone cluster) | X |
| Hosted control planes | X |
| Multi node, Compact (three node), or Single node (SNO), or all | X |
| Connected / Restricted Network | X |
| Architectures, e.g. x86_x64, ARM (aarch64), IBM Power (ppc64le), and IBM Z (s390x) | Minimal: x86_64. Ideal: also aarch64. Optimal: all |
| Operator compatibility | X |
| Backport needed (list applicable versions) | No |
| UI need (e.g. OpenShift Console, dynamic plugin, OCM) | No |
| Other (please specify) | N/A |

h3. *Documentation Considerations*

* *PQC and FIPS are mutually exclusive* until all components build on UBI 10
* Customers should plan adequate *maintenance windows* as TLS setting changes will cause component restarts
* The overall TLS adherence and PQC posture should be documented consistently in a single place

items.toString:
h3. *Feature Overview (aka. Goal Summary)*

This feature aims to ensure that once all Platform Agnostic and Rolling Streams operator teams have completed their TLS consistency/ML-KEM development and per-component testing, the resulting cluster (sum of all parts) does indeed behave as intended: TLS 1.3 with hybrid ML-KEM being the default offered key encapsulation protocol. This is a test activity only.

h3. *Goals (aka. expected user outcomes)*

A newly deployed OCP 5.0 cluster should use quantum-safe key encapsulation by default for all TLS connections served by Platform Agnostic and Rolling Streams operators.

h3. *Requirements (aka. Acceptance Criteria):*

Once an OCP 5.0 cluster is up and running, a CI job can scan all discoverable service endpoints exposed by Platform Agnostic and Rolling Streams operators to ensure they're using TLS 1.3 (required for PQC support), and then run a series of smoke tests to validate basic functionality while in PQC-mode.

h3. *Testing Approaches*

Teams should validate ML-KEM support using one or more of these approaches:

# *Cluster-wide scan* - tls-scanner periodic CI covers basic cluster installation
# *Namespace-specific scan* - Layered products should point tls-scanner at their namespace during integration testing
# *Dedicated functional tests* - Required for short-lived/transient TLS endpoints that the scanner cannot reliably catch

{warning}The tls-scanner cannot guarantee it will find transient endpoints. Teams must add dedicated testing for any TLS servers that spin up/down during normal operations.{warning}

*Deployment considerations:*

|*Deployment considerations*|*List applicable specific needs (N/A = not applicable)*|
|Self-managed, managed, or both|X|
|Classic (standalone cluster)|X|
|Hosted control planes|X|
|Multi node, Compact (three node), or Single node (SNO), or all|X|
|Connected / Restricted Network|X|
|Architectures, e.g. x86_x64, ARM (aarch64), IBM Power (ppc64le), and IBM Z (s390x)|Minimal: x86_64. Ideal: also aarch64. Optimal: all|
|Operator compatibility|X|
|Backport needed (list applicable versions)|No|
|UI need (e.g. OpenShift Console, dynamic plugin, OCM)|No|
|Other (please specify)|N/A|

h3. *Documentation Considerations*

* *PQC and FIPS are mutually exclusive* until all components build on UBI 10
* Customers should plan adequate *maintenance windows* as TLS setting changes will cause component restarts
* The overall TLS adherence and PQC posture should be documented consistently in a single place

h3. *Key Contacts*

* Jean-Philippe Jung (jjung@redhat.com) - PQC Lead / Feature Owner
* Joe Lanford (jlanford@redhat.com) - Engineering Lead
* Lance Bragstad (lbragsta@redhat.com) - Engineering (tls-scanner)
* Mike Fiedler (mfiedler@redhat.com) - QE Lead
* Ashley Hardin (ahardin@redhat.com) - Docs Lead
* Josh Beverly (jbeverly@redhat.com) - SET Lead

Questions? Reach out in [#forum-ocp-tls-strict-obedience|https://redhat.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C098FU5MRAB].

h3. *Definition of Done*

The onboarding template [PLMPGM-7881|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/PLMPGM-7881] is the official ML-KEM testing onboarding template. For this scope, teams should target support no later than their first release after *OCP 5.0 GA*. Teams in the Platform Agnostic and Rolling Streams scope should clone this template and link back to this OCPSTRAT issue (instead of [OCPSTRAT-2361]).

# Team clones [PLMPGM-7881|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/PLMPGM-7881] template (Epic + child tasks) via *More > Clone EPIC and Children*
# Cloned Epic and child tasks are moved to the team's own Jira project via Bulk Edit
# Cloned Epic is linked to this OCPSTRAT Feature issue using *Is Triggered By* link type
# Team completes all child tasks within the cloned Epic (ML-KEM validation, tls-scanner testing, etc.)
# Cloned Epic is transitioned to *Closed / Complete*
# All Platform Agnostic and Rolling Streams operator cloned Epics are Closed - this Feature can then be closed

h3. *Out of Scope*

* Core and Platform Aligned operators (see [OCPSTRAT-2361|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCPSTRAT-2361])
* Outbound TLS connections
* Converting HTTP traffic to HTTPS (recommended to track separately as good security practice)

h3. *Related Work*

* [OCPSTRAT-2611|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCPSTRAT-2611] - TLSadherence field must be enabled as part of OCP 5.0 cycle
* [OCPSTRAT-3145|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCPSTRAT-3145] - Further restricting key exchange groups (OCP 5.1 roadmap)

h3. *Resources*

* TLS Profile Compliance — Implementation Reference
* Slack: [#forum-ocp-tls-strict-obedience|https://redhat.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C098FU5MRAB]

h2. Goal

Make the Red Hat build of Kueue's {{waitForPodsReady}} timeout configurable (starting with a global operator-level setting) so workloads with long initialization phases are not incorrectly timed out.

h2. Background

Source RFE: [RFE-9252|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RFE-9252]

RHBoK currently hardcodes a 5-minute timeout ([operator configmap|https://github.com/openshift/kueue-operator/blob/main/pkg/configmap/configmap.go#L139]). Upstream workload-level annotation support is tracked in [kubernetes-sigs/kueue#4803|https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/issues/4803].

h2. Customer Impact

* Customer *Telenor* has requested this capability
* AI/ML and batch workloads often exceed 5 minutes to reach Ready due to large image pulls, heavy init containers, or GPU provisioning delays
* Exceeding the limit causes false failures, restarts, and resource churn

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* [ ] Cluster administrators can configure a global {{waitForPodsReady}} timeout via the Kueue operator API
* [ ] Default remains backward compatible with the current 5-minute timeout
* [ ] Operator configuration is documented
* [ ] (Stretch/follow-up) Workload-level override via annotations when upstream support is available

h2. Technical Approach

_To be refined — see {{rfe-strat-refine}} skill._

h2. Dependencies

Upstream annotation support: [kubernetes-sigs/kueue#4803|https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/issues/4803]

items.fromString:
h3. *Feature Overview (aka. Goal Summary)*

As a managed service operator (ROSA HCP, ARO HCP) or self-managed HyperShift administrator, I want non-disruptive configuration changes to be delivered to existing worker nodes in-place — without node replacement, drain, or reboot — regardless of the NodePool's upgrade strategy (Replace or InPlace).

Today, when configuration changes are excluded from triggering a Replace rollout (see OCPSTRAT-3298 — Predictable NodePool Rollout Control), existing worker nodes retain their original configuration until the next spec-driven rollout occurs. This means management-side updates such as image digest bumps, SSH key rotations, trust bundle updates, and registry mirror changes are not applied to running nodes until a full rollout is triggered by an unrelated spec change.

This feature introduces a config refresh mechanism that uses the Machine Config Daemon (MCD) with Node Disruption Policies (NDPs) to apply eligible configuration changes to existing nodes without disruption. Changes that would require a reboot (kernel arguments, FIPS, OS image, etc.) are excluded from the refresh path and continue to require a Replace rollout.

h3. *Goals (aka. expected user outcomes)*

* Non-disruptive configuration changes MUST be delivered to existing worker nodes without node replacement, drain, or reboot
* The config refresh mechanism MUST work for NodePools with Replace upgrade strategy (MachineDeployment-managed nodes), not just InPlace
* The mechanism MUST guarantee no node reboots by validating all changes against Node Disruption Policies before applying
* Changes that require a reboot MUST be excluded from the refresh path and deferred to the next Replace rollout

h3. *Requirements (aka. Acceptance Criteria)*

# A new config refresh mechanism MUST deliver non-disruptive configuration changes to existing worker nodes regardless of the NodePool's upgrade strategy (Replace or InPlace).
# The config refresh mechanism MUST use the Machine Config Daemon (MCD) to apply file changes to nodes, leveraging MCD's existing infrastructure for file writing, state tracking, and completion reporting.
# HyperShift (via the HCCO — Hosted Cluster Config Operator) MUST configure Node Disruption Policies (NDPs) in the guest cluster for all file paths managed by HyperShift's core ignition configs, ensuring MCD applies these changes without draining or rebooting nodes.
# The config refresh controller MUST validate that every file in the diff maps to a non-reboot NDP action before sending the diff to MCD. If any change would trigger a reboot, the change MUST be excluded from the refresh and held for the next Replace rollout.
# The following categories of changes MUST be eligible for in-place config refresh (no reboot, no drain):
#* Management-side container image references in static pod manifests (e.g., HAProxy image in {{/etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver-proxy.yaml}})
#* SSH authorized key changes ({{passwd.users.sshAuthorizedKeys}}) — MCD default NDP action: {{None}}
#* Additional trust bundle / CA certificate changes ({{/etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/}}) — MCD default NDP action: {{Restart update-ca-trust + crio}}
#* Registry mirror configuration changes ({{/etc/containers/registries.conf}}, {{/etc/containers/registries.d/}}) — MCD default NDP action: {{Reload crio}} / {{Special}}
#* Pull secret changes ({{/var/lib/kubelet/config.json}}) — MCD default NDP action: {{None}}
#* HAProxy configuration changes ({{/etc/kubernetes/apiserver-proxy-config/haproxy.cfg}})
#* API server IP setup/teardown scripts ({{/usr/local/bin/setup-apiserver-ip.sh}}, {{/usr/local/bin/teardown-apiserver-ip.sh}})
# The following categories of changes MUST NOT be eligible for in-place config refresh and MUST continue to require a Replace rollout:
#* FIPS mode changes (hardcoded reboot in MCD, irreconcilable)
#* Kernel argument changes (hardcoded reboot in MCD)
#* OS image changes (hardcoded reboot in MCD)
#* Kernel type changes — realtime, 64k-pages (hardcoded reboot in MCD)
#* RPM extension changes (hardcoded reboot in MCD)
#* Systemd unit changes with no safe NDP
#* Release image version changes (full upgrade lifecycle)
# The config refresh mechanism MUST respect {{maxUnavailable}} settings to pace updates across nodes, preventing simultaneous MCD operations on all nodes.
# Config refresh state MUST be tracked via separate annotations from the Replace/InPlace upgrade state, so the two mechanisms do not interfere with each other.
# NodePool status SHOULD report the refresh state, indicating whether nodes are up-to-date with the latest non-disruptive config or have a refresh pending.

h3. *Background and Motivation*

*Dependency*

This feature builds on OCPSTRAT-3298 (Predictable NodePool Rollout Control), which introduces a rollout hash split separating spec-driven changes from management-side changes. OCPSTRAT-3298 prevents unexpected rollouts but does not deliver the excluded changes to existing nodes. This feature closes that gap.

*Problem Statement*

After OCPSTRAT-3298, management-side changes (image bumps, registry overrides) no longer trigger Replace rollouts. However, existing nodes and new scale-up nodes continue running with the old configuration until the next spec-driven rollout. For some changes this is acceptable (an old HAProxy image still works), but for others — SSH key rotations, trust bundle updates, pull secret changes — timely delivery to running nodes is important.

HyperShift's existing in-place upgrader (used for NodePools with InPlace upgrade strategy) already demonstrates the pattern: it creates MCD pods per node that apply configuration changes on the host. This feature generalizes that pattern to all NodePools and restricts it to non-disruptive changes.

*MCD and Node Disruption Policies*

The Machine Config Daemon determines its post-apply action (reboot, drain, restart service, or none) based on Node Disruption Policies. The MCD's decision flow:

# Changes to OS image, kernel args, FIPS, kernel type, or extensions — *hardcoded reboot*, no NDP can override
# File changes — matched against NDP file policies by path; unmatched paths default to *reboot*
# Systemd unit changes — matched against NDP unit policies; unmatched units default to *reboot*
# SSH key changes — default NDP action: *None*

For the config refresh use case, HyperShift must configure NDPs for all file paths it manages that lack a safe default, and must never send changes through the refresh path that would hit the hardcoded reboot cases.

h3. *Design Details*

*Node Disruption Policy configuration*

The HCCO configures a {{MachineConfiguration}} resource in the guest cluster with NDPs for HyperShift-managed file paths that lack safe defaults:

{code:yaml}spec:
  nodeDisruptionPolicy:
    files:
    - path: /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver-proxy.yaml
      actions:
      - type: None
    - path: /etc/kubernetes/apiserver-proxy-config/haproxy.cfg
      actions:
      - type: None
    - path: /usr/local/bin/setup-apiserver-ip.sh
      actions:
      - type: None
    - path: /usr/local/bin/teardown-apiserver-ip.sh
      actions:
      - type: None{code}

Paths with existing safe defaults (SSH keys, trust bundles, registry config, pull secret) do not need additional NDP entries.

*Config refresh controller*

A new controller (or extension of the existing in-place upgrader in the HCCO) that:

# Watches Nodes and Machines associated with all NodePools (not just InPlace-strategy ones)
# Detects when the payload hash has changed but the rollout hash has not (using the hash split from OCPSTRAT-3298)
# Computes the file-level diff and validates all changed paths have non-reboot NDPs
# Delivers the updated config to nodes via MCD pods (same mechanism as the existing in-place upgrader)
# Tracks refresh state via a dedicated annotation (e.g., {{hypershift.openshift.io/currentRefreshConfig}})
# Respects {{maxUnavailable}} for pacing

*Safety invariant*

Before sending any diff to MCD, the controller verifies:

* {{diff.osUpdate == false}}
* {{diff.kargs == false}}
* {{diff.fips == false}}
* {{diff.kernelType == false}}
* {{diff.extensions == false}}
* Every changed file path matches a NDP with action {{None}}, {{Restart}}, {{Reload}}, or {{DaemonReload}} — never {{Reboot}}
* No systemd unit changes are present (unless covered by a non-reboot NDP)

If any condition fails, the refresh is skipped and the change is deferred to the next Replace rollout.

h3. *Deployment Considerations*

||*Deployment consideration*||*Applicability*||
|Self-managed, managed, or both|Both|
|Classic (standalone cluster)|N/A (HyperShift only)|
|Hosted control planes|Yes — primary target|
|Multi node, Compact (three node), or Single node (SNO), or all|All (applies to worker NodePools)|
|Connected / Restricted Network|Both|
|Architectures|All (x86_64, ARM, IBM Power, IBM Z)|
|Platforms|All HyperShift platforms (AWS, Azure, KubeVirt, IBM Cloud, OpenStack, Agent)|
|Operator compatibility|Requires MCO with Node Disruption Policy support (OCP 4.14+)|
|Backport needed|No|
|UI need|No|

h3. *Risks and Mitigations*

||*Risk*||*Impact*||*Mitigation*||
|MCD reboots node during config refresh|Customer workload disruption|Safety invariant check validates all changed paths have non-reboot NDPs before invoking MCD; refresh skipped if any path would reboot|
|NDP not configured before MCD runs|MCD falls back to reboot for unmatched paths|HCCO ensures NDP is configured as prerequisite; refresh controller validates NDP exists before proceeding|
|MCD pod fails or hangs on a node|Node stuck in refresh state|Timeout and retry logic with maxUnavailable pacing prevents fleet-wide impact; degraded state surfaced in NodePool status|
|Interaction between config refresh and concurrent Replace rollout|Race condition on node state|Refresh annotations are separate from upgrade annotations; refresh controller skips nodes that are pending Replace|

h3. *Test Plan*

* *Unit tests*: Verify safety invariant rejects changes that would reboot (OS image, kargs, FIPS, unmatched file paths)
* *Unit tests*: Verify safety invariant accepts changes for paths with non-reboot NDPs
* *E2E test*: Verify config refresh delivers updated static pod manifest to existing Replace-strategy nodes without reboot
* *E2E test*: Verify SSH key rotation is applied in-place without node replacement
* *E2E test*: Verify trust bundle update is applied in-place with crio restart but no reboot
* *E2E test*: Verify changes requiring reboot are excluded from refresh and deferred

|Interaction between config refresh and concurrent Replace rollout|Race condition on node state|Refresh annotations are separate from upgrade annotations; refresh controller skips nodes that are pending Replace|

h3. *Test Plan*

* *Unit tests*: Verify safety invariant rejects changes that would reboot (OS image, kargs, FIPS, unmatched file paths)
* *Unit tests*: Verify safety invariant accepts changes for paths with non-reboot NDPs
* *E2E test*: Verify config refresh delivers updated static pod manifest to existing Replace-strategy nodes without reboot
* *E2E test*: Verify SSH key rotation is applied in-place without node replacement
* *E2E test*: Verify trust bundle update is applied in-place with crio restart but no reboot
* *E2E test*: Verify changes requiring reboot are excluded from refresh and deferred

h3. *Feature Overview (aka. Goal Summary)*

As a managed service operator (ROSA HCP, ARO HCP) or self-managed HyperShift administrator, I want non-disruptive configuration changes to be delivered to existing worker nodes in-place — without node replacement, drain, or reboot — regardless of the NodePool's upgrade strategy (Replace or InPlace).

Today, when configuration changes are excluded from triggering a Replace rollout (see OCPSTRAT-3298 — Predictable NodePool Rollout Control), existing worker nodes retain their original configuration until the next spec-driven rollout occurs. This means management-side updates such as image digest bumps, SSH key rotations, trust bundle updates, and registry mirror changes are not applied to running nodes until a full rollout is triggered by an unrelated spec change.

This feature introduces a config refresh mechanism that uses the Machine Config Daemon (MCD) with Node Disruption Policies (NDPs) to apply eligible configuration changes to existing nodes without disruption. Changes that would require a reboot (kernel arguments, FIPS, OS image, etc.) are excluded from the refresh path and continue to require a Replace rollout.

h3. *Goals (aka. expected user outcomes)*

* Non-disruptive configuration changes MUST be delivered to existing worker nodes without node replacement, drain, or reboot
* The config refresh mechanism MUST work for NodePools with Replace upgrade strategy (MachineDeployment-managed nodes), not just InPlace
* The mechanism MUST guarantee no node reboots by validating all changes against Node Disruption Policies before applying
* Changes that require a reboot MUST be excluded from the refresh path and deferred to the next Replace rollout

h3. *Requirements (aka. Acceptance Criteria)*

# A new config refresh mechanism MUST deliver non-disruptive configuration changes to existing worker nodes regardless of the NodePool's upgrade strategy (Replace or InPlace).
# The config refresh mechanism MUST use the Machine Config Daemon (MCD) to apply file changes to nodes, leveraging MCD's existing infrastructure for file writing, state tracking, and completion reporting.
# HyperShift (via the HCCO — Hosted Cluster Config Operator) MUST configure Node Disruption Policies (NDPs) in the guest cluster for all file paths managed by HyperShift's core ignition configs, ensuring MCD applies these changes without draining or rebooting nodes.
# The config refresh controller MUST validate that every file in the diff maps to a non-reboot NDP action before sending the diff to MCD. If any change would trigger a reboot, the change MUST be excluded from the refresh and held for the next Replace rollout.
# The following categories of changes MUST be eligible for in-place config refresh (no reboot, no drain):
#* Management-side container image references in static pod manifests (e.g., HAProxy image in {{/etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver-proxy.yaml}})
#* SSH authorized key changes ({{passwd.users.sshAuthorizedKeys}}) — MCD default NDP action: {{None}}
#* Additional trust bundle / CA certificate changes ({{/etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/}}) — MCD default NDP action: {{Restart update-ca-trust + crio}}
#* Registry mirror configuration changes ({{/etc/containers/registries.conf}}, {{/etc/containers/registries.d/}}) — MCD default NDP action: {{Reload crio}} / {{Special}}
#* Pull secret changes ({{/var/lib/kubelet/config.json}}) — MCD default NDP action: {{None}}
#* HAProxy configuration changes ({{/etc/kubernetes/apiserver-proxy-config/haproxy.cfg}})
#* API server IP setup/teardown scripts ({{/usr/local/bin/setup-apiserver-ip.sh}}, {{/usr/local/bin/teardown-apiserver-ip.sh}})
# The following categories of changes MUST NOT be eligible for in-place config refresh and MUST continue to require a Replace rollout:
#* FIPS mode changes (hardcoded reboot in MCD, irreconcilable)
#* Kernel argument changes (hardcoded reboot in MCD)
#* OS image changes (hardcoded reboot in MCD)
#* Kernel type changes — realtime, 64k-pages (hardcoded reboot in MCD)
#* RPM extension changes (hardcoded reboot in MCD)
#* Systemd unit changes with no safe NDP
#* Release image version changes (full upgrade lifecycle)
# The config refresh mechanism MUST respect {{maxUnavailable}} settings to pace updates across nodes, preventing simultaneous MCD operations on all nodes.
# Config refresh state MUST be tracked via separate annotations from the Replace/InPlace upgrade state, so the two mechanisms do not interfere with each other.
# NodePool status SHOULD report the refresh state, indicating whether nodes are up-to-date with the latest non-disruptive config or have a refresh pending.

h3. *Background and Motivation*

*Dependency*

This feature builds on OCPSTRAT-3298 (Predictable NodePool Rollout Control), which introduces a rollout hash split separating spec-driven changes from management-side changes. OCPSTRAT-3298 prevents unexpected rollouts but does not deliver the excluded changes to existing nodes. This feature closes that gap.

*Problem Statement*

After OCPSTRAT-3298, management-side changes (image bumps, registry overrides) no longer trigger Replace rollouts. However, existing nodes and new scale-up nodes continue running with the old configuration until the next spec-driven rollout. For some changes this is acceptable (an old HAProxy image still works), but for others — SSH key rotations, trust bundle updates, pull secret changes — timely delivery to running nodes is important.

HyperShift's existing in-place upgrader (used for NodePools with InPlace upgrade strategy) already demonstrates the pattern: it creates MCD pods per node that apply configuration changes on the host. This feature generalizes that pattern to all NodePools and restricts it to non-disruptive changes.

*MCD and Node Disruption Policies*

The Machine Config Daemon determines its post-apply action (reboot, drain, restart service, or none) based on Node Disruption Policies. The MCD's decision flow:

# Changes to OS image, kernel args, FIPS, kernel type, or extensions — *hardcoded reboot*, no NDP can override
# File changes — matched against NDP file policies by path; unmatched paths default to *reboot*
# Systemd unit changes — matched against NDP unit policies; unmatched units default to *reboot*
# SSH key changes — default NDP action: *None*

For the config refresh use case, HyperShift must configure NDPs for all file paths it manages that lack a safe default, and must never send changes through the refresh path that would hit the hardcoded reboot cases.

h3. *Design Details*

*Node Disruption Policy configuration*

The HCCO configures a {{MachineConfiguration}} resource in the guest cluster with NDPs for HyperShift-managed file paths that lack safe defaults:

{code:yaml}spec:
  nodeDisruptionPolicy:
    files:
    - path: /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver-proxy.yaml
      actions:
      - type: None
    - path: /etc/kubernetes/apiserver-proxy-config/haproxy.cfg
      actions:
      - type: None
    - path: /usr/local/bin/setup-apiserver-ip.sh
      actions:
      - type: None
    - path: /usr/local/bin/teardown-apiserver-ip.sh
      actions:
      - type: None{code}

Paths with existing safe defaults (SSH keys, trust bundles, registry config, pull secret) do not need additional NDP entries.

*Config refresh controller*

A new controller (or extension of the existing in-place upgrader in the HCCO) that:

# Watches Nodes and Machines associated with all NodePools (not just InPlace-strategy ones)
# Detects when the payload hash has changed but the rollout hash has not (using the hash split from OCPSTRAT-3298)
# Computes the file-level diff and validates all changed paths have non-reboot NDPs
# Delivers the updated config to nodes via MCD pods (same mechanism as the existing in-place upgrader)
# Tracks refresh state via a dedicated annotation (e.g., {{hypershift.openshift.io/currentRefreshConfig}})
# Respects {{maxUnavailable}} for pacing

*Safety invariant*

Before sending any diff to MCD, the controller verifies:

* {{diff.osUpdate == false}}
* {{diff.kargs == false}}
* {{diff.fips == false}}
* {{diff.kernelType == false}}
* {{diff.extensions == false}}
* Every changed file path matches a NDP with action {{None}}, {{Restart}}, {{Reload}}, or {{DaemonReload}} — never {{Reboot}}
* No systemd unit changes are present (unless covered by a non-reboot NDP)

If any condition fails, the refresh is skipped and the change is deferred to the next Replace rollout.

h3. *Deployment Considerations*

||*Deployment consideration*||*Applicability*||
|Self-managed, managed, or both|Both|
|Classic (standalone cluster)|N/A (HyperShift only)|
|Hosted control planes|Yes — primary target|
|Multi node, Compact (three node), or Single node (SNO), or all|All (applies to worker NodePools)|
|Connected / Restricted Network|Both|
|Architectures|All (x86_64, ARM, IBM Power, IBM Z)|
|Platforms|All HyperShift platforms (AWS, Azure, KubeVirt, IBM Cloud, OpenStack, Agent)|
|Operator compatibility|Requires MCO with Node Disruption Policy support (OCP 4.14+)|
|Backport needed|No|
|UI need|No|

h3. *Risks and Mitigations*

||*Risk*||*Impact*||*Mitigation*||
|MCD reboots node during config refresh|Customer workload disruption|Safety invariant check validates all changed paths have non-reboot NDPs before invoking MCD; refresh skipped if any path would reboot|
|NDP not configured before MCD runs|MCD falls back to reboot for unmatched paths|HCCO ensures NDP is configured as prerequisite; refresh controller validates NDP exists before proceeding|
|MCD pod fails or hangs on a node|Node stuck in refresh state|Timeout and retry logic with maxUnavailable pacing prevents fleet-wide impact; degraded state surfaced in NodePool status|
|Interaction between config refresh and concurrent Replace rollout|Race condition on node state|Refresh annotations are separate from upgrade annotations; refresh controller skips nodes that are pending Replace|

h3. *Test Plan*

* *Unit tests*: Verify safety invariant rejects changes that would reboot (OS image, kargs, FIPS, unmatched file paths)
* *Unit tests*: Verify safety invariant accepts changes for paths with non-reboot NDPs
* *E2E test*: Verify config refresh delivers updated static pod manifest to existing Replace-strategy nodes without reboot
* *E2E test*: Verify SSH key rotation is applied in-place without node replacement
* *E2E test*: Verify trust bundle update is applied in-place with crio restart but no reboot
* *E2E test*: Verify changes requiring reboot are excluded from refresh and deferred
